clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant ataxia whose hallmark is early, prominent dysphonia — a strained, spasmodic voice that often precedes or overshadows limb ataxia.
Palatal tremor (palatal myoclonus) is a characteristic and unusual accompanying feature.
Calcification of the dentate nucleus is frequently visible on CT and provides a valuable radiological clue.
Caused by a small contiguous duplication (a copy-number gain) on chromosome 11q12, rather than by a repeat expansion.
Progression is slow, and gaze-evoked nystagmus and mild pyramidal signs may be present.
The phenotype was originally described in an Australian family of Anglo-Celtic descent.
Because the early voice change can resemble primary spasmodic dysphonia, the diagnosis may be missed before ataxia becomes evident.
reference.pathophysiology: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 20 is an autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia caused by a small contiguous duplication, a copy-number gain, on chromosome 11q12, which distinguishes it mechanistically from the trinucleotide and pentanucleotide repeat-expansion ataxias. The gene or genes responsible for the phenotype through a dosage effect are not fully defined, with overexpression of genes within the duplicated segment (a proposed candidate being DAGLA, which encodes diacylglycerol lipase alpha) implicated. The disorder is marked radiologically by calcification of the dentate nucleus and clinically by early bulbar involvement — spasmodic dysphonia and palatal tremor — together with slowly progressive cerebellar ataxia.
additionalDifferentials: Other autosomal dominant SCAs presenting with early dysarthria, such as SCA1
SCA36, which can produce bulbar features and tongue involvement
Progressive ataxia with palatal tremor of other genetic or sporadic cause
Primary or idiopathic spasmodic dysphonia before cerebellar signs emerge
Primary familial brain calcification and other causes of intracranial calcification
Dominant ataxias featuring cortical or action myoclonus
additionalInvestigations: CT head to detect calcification of the dentate nucleus
MRI brain to assess cerebellar atrophy
Molecular testing by chromosomal microarray or MLPA to detect the 11q12 duplication (dosage-sensitive methods)
Hereditary ataxia gene panel to exclude repeat-expansion subtypes
Laryngoscopy and formal voice assessment for the dysphonia
Evaluation for other causes of intracranial calcification (calcium-phosphate and parathyroid indices)
Family pedigree analysis with genetic counselling
redFlags: Rapidly worsening dysphonia or dysphagia with aspiration risk.
New cognitive, psychiatric or extrapyramidal features suggesting an alternative diagnosis.
Frequent falls as cerebellar ataxia advances.
Extensive intracranial calcification beyond the dentate raising other metabolic disorders.
reference.prognosis: Slowly progressive over years to decades, with disability dominated by cerebellar ataxia and bulbar dysfunction; lifespan is usually preserved.
pitfalls: Attributing the early voice change to a primary laryngeal disorder and missing the underlying ataxia.
Expecting a repeat expansion and failing to test for the duplication, which requires dosage-sensitive or array methods.
Overlooking dentate nucleus calcification on imaging.
Confusing the condition with sporadic progressive ataxia with palatal tremor.
references: Neurogenetics reference texts on autosomal dominant spinocerebellar ataxias
Standard neurology textbook chapters on inherited ataxias
Consensus reviews of copy-number and non-repeat cerebellar ataxias
management: With no disease-modifying therapy, anchor care on physiotherapy for gait and balance, occupational therapy, and speech and language therapy
Treat the spasmodic dysphonia with laryngeal botulinum toxin injections alongside ENT/laryngology and voice therapy
Manage palatal tremor symptomatically where it is troublesome or causes ear click
Institute falls prevention and provide mobility aids for progressive gait ataxia
Confirm the dentate calcification is not attributable to a treatable metabolic cause by checking calcium, phosphate and parathyroid status
Monitor for bulbar dysfunction with periodic swallow assessment
Offer genetic counselling and cascade testing using dosage-sensitive methods (chromosomal microarray or MLPA) to detect the 11q12 duplication
